holdings.thesis: HOLD: shares ~$418, still within the $412-$430 range from earlier this week -- no new deterioration. Lake Street upgraded to Buy from Hold (9/3) and Goldman Sachs reiterated Buy after the Q2 FY27 EBITDA beat and Power-segment margin outperformance; both are incremental positive analyst sentiment, not new negative data. Still down -32.0% vs. cost basis on stop-loss review (legacy of original entry price), but position stays small (3.1% of portfolio) after two prior trims and no fresh catalyst warrants a further cut.

HOLD: shares ~$171, up modestly from Friday's ~$164 close. No new information since the 9/1 guidance-miss selloff already reflected in the three prior trims; BofA's $275 PT (Buy maintained) and FY27 guidance implying 85%+ revenue growth remain the known bull case supporting the now much-smaller (5.4%) position. Holding the de-risked remainder absent fresh negative data.

HOLD: thesis intact; shares ~$154, holding most of the gains from Evercore's 9/1 Outperform/$210 upgrade and DA Davidson's $175 PT. The earnings-decline flag remains attributable to AI-feature reinvestment rather than demand softness (DAUs +23% YoY, paid subscribers +17%). Position at 14.9% of portfolio, just under the 15% max_position_pct cap -- watching for a forced trim if price appreciates further.

HOLD: shares ~$55.66, roughly flat. A new Form 4 shows Director Louise Forlenza sold 10,000 shares on 9/4, adding to the known insider-selling pattern already reflected in the two prior trims (~85% combined reduction); position is already minimal (1.4% of portfolio) so a further trim isn't warranted for an incremental data point of this size. CEO succession (Singhal to CEO effective 9/30) remains known and unchanged.

HOLD: material new positive -- Vertiv agreed to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for ~$1.45B cash (plus up to $1.15B in EBITDA-linked earnouts) to accelerate power deployment for AI data centers, closing Q4 2026; shares rose to ~$280.53 on the news, and the company declared its regular $0.062 quarterly dividend (ex-date 9/14). The Hagens Berman/Pomerantz securities-fraud investigations remain a known, unchanged overhang. Position now 13.25% of portfolio, under the 15% cap after prior trims -- no action needed.

HOLD: new positive catalyst -- a federal judge rejected the DOJ's push to force Alphabet to divest its ad exchange, a meaningful antitrust win that reduces a known regulatory overhang. Gemini 3.8 Flash rollout continues and Berkshire's Greg Abel reiterated Alphabet as a 'significant AI player.' Shares ~$338, up 8.5% YTD; thesis intact.

HOLD: no material new catalyst -- the FTC/22-state ad-pricing lawsuit (filed 9/1) and broader e-commerce layoff headlines remain the known drivers of the ~11% pullback from August's all-time high. Q2 fundamentals (revenue +20% YoY constant-currency, operating margin 13.7% vs 11.4% a year ago) still support the thesis; Rosenblatt's Buy/$335 PT unchanged.

HOLD: no new catalyst beyond already-known items (Piper Sandler's $185 PT from 9/3, Q3 dividend of $1.03/share payable 9/10). ExxonMobil confirmed as operator of the Papua LNG project with reduced estimated capex ($14B), a modest incremental positive. Thesis intact, no action needed.

HOLD: thesis intact -- Truist raised its PT to $85 (from $83), continuing the wave of post-earnings target hikes (Goldman $115, Bernstein $110). CEO Levchin's fireside chat at Goldman's Communacopia + Technology Conference (9/8, 3:05pm PT) is the next near-term catalyst to watch; no new negative data today.

HOLD: mixed but not thesis-breaking -- new insider-selling headlines surfaced 9/5 (Datadog grouped with PDD/Roblox/TI/Fastly in a sell-off report), a data point to keep watching, but position is small (3.7% of portfolio) and a separate analyst framework raised its fair-value estimate to ~$317 from ~$268. The known OpenAI spend-deceleration flag from the Q2 call remains the primary driver of the post-earnings pullback, not fresh fundamental deterioration.

HOLD: thesis intact -- a new Phase 1 Tirzepatide-based Type 1 diabetes study adds pipeline optionality alongside the core GLP-1 franchise and the pending $2.88B Merida Biosciences acquisition. Buy consensus ($1,302.60 PT, 20 analysts) unchanged; Lilly presents at Morgan Stanley's healthcare conference on 9/14.

HOLD: thesis strengthening -- a new Notre Dame partnership adds a fresh distribution/brand catalyst alongside the known Kraken stablecoin deal. This week's Scotiabank (Outperform/$25 PT) and Piper Sandler (Overweight/$22 PT) initiations remain supportive; CEO Noto's fireside chat at Goldman's Communacopia conference (9/8) is the next watch item for credit-quality/growth commentary.

HOLD: thesis intact -- Bernstein maintained a Hold rating (9/3, not a downgrade from an existing Buy) and CEO Creed's insider stock sale (9/1) is a known, modest data point that doesn't indicate deteriorating fundamentals given the record $72B backlog and ongoing FieldAI physical-AI/robotics partnership. No new negative catalyst.

HOLD: thesis intact -- IonQ's investor day on 9/8 could bring multi-year revenue guidance, a near-term catalyst to watch. Record Q2 revenue growth of 287% YoY remains the core support; participation in Quantum World Congress 2026 (9/23-25) is a minor known event. Position stays modest (2.3% of portfolio) given the company's pre-profit risk profile.
